SL-C02-COOKIE-01.title: The login cookie is missing security protections
SL-C02-COOKIE-01.what: A cookie used to keep a visitor signed in is missing one or more browser protections. The evidence shows which settings are missing.
SL-C02-COOKIE-01.why: Depending on the missing setting, a malicious page script or an insecure connection could expose the cookie. A stolen, still-valid cookie could let someone use that session.
SL-C02-COOKIE-01.fix: Add Secure, HttpOnly, and an appropriate SameSite setting to session cookies.
SL-C02-COOKIE-01.limit: We checked cookie settings. We did not demonstrate stealing a cookie, guessing passwords, or bypassing the login.

SL-C04-CSP-01.title: The browser is missing a guard against harmful scripts
SL-C04-CSP-01.what: The checked pages do not have an effective Content-Security-Policy. This is a browser rule that restricts which scripts may run.
SL-C04-CSP-01.why: If someone finds a separate script-injection flaw, this missing protection can make it easier for their script to run on your pages.
SL-C04-CSP-01.fix: Configure and enforce a Content-Security-Policy that allows only required scripts and sources.
SL-C04-CSP-01.limit: A missing policy is not proof of script injection or account takeover.

SL-C04-FRAME-01.title: Another website may be able to put your page inside its own page
SL-C04-FRAME-01.what: The responses are missing effective rules that restrict which websites can embed these pages.
SL-C04-FRAME-01.why: Someone could disguise an embedded page and trick a signed-in visitor into clicking a real button. The impact depends on what actions that page allows.
SL-C04-FRAME-01.fix: Add CSP frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options to restrict embedding.
SL-C04-FRAME-01.limit: We checked embedding protections. We did not demonstrate a harmful click or a change to an account.

SL-C04-REFERRER-01.title: Your pages do not set a rule for sharing the visitor’s previous address
SL-C04-REFERRER-01.what: The checked responses do not set Referrer-Policy, which tells the browser how much of the previous page address to send.
SL-C04-REFERRER-01.why: If a page address contains sensitive details, those details might be shared with another website. Modern browser defaults can reduce this risk.
SL-C04-REFERRER-01.fix: Set Referrer-Policy to strict-origin-when-cross-origin, or a stricter policy appropriate for the site.
SL-C04-REFERRER-01.limit: We did not demonstrate a password, token, or private record being leaked.

SL-C06-COMPONENT-01.title: A library version may have a known security issue
SL-C06-COMPONENT-01.what: A library version seen in the page matches a published security advisory in the scanner’s saved advisory list.
SL-C06-COMPONENT-01.why: If the detected version is correct, the fix is absent, and the vulnerable feature is used, someone may be able to exploit the issue described in that advisory.
SL-C06-COMPONENT-01.fix: Verify the actual installed build and advisory conditions, then update or apply the vendor fix.
SL-C06-COMPONENT-01.limit: A version match is a lead, not proof of exploitation. We did not demonstrate a login bypass or access to private records.

SL-C01-TLS-01.title: The secure connection has a certificate or encryption problem
SL-C01-TLS-01.what: The connection check found an issue with the certificate, its expiry, or the supported encryption settings. The evidence identifies the specific issue.
SL-C01-TLS-01.why: Visitors may see security warnings. Certain weak connection settings can also make interception easier, depending on the issue.
SL-C01-TLS-01.fix: Install and renew a trusted certificate for this hostname and remove obsolete TLS versions.
SL-C01-TLS-01.limit: The finding does not prove that traffic was intercepted.

SL-C01-REDIR-01.title: The website can serve a page without encryption
SL-C01-REDIR-01.what: The HTTP address returned an application page instead of sending the visitor to HTTPS.
SL-C01-REDIR-01.why: Anyone able to observe or alter that unencrypted connection may read or change data sent over it.
SL-C01-REDIR-01.fix: Redirect HTTP requests to HTTPS and use HTTPS in links.
SL-C01-REDIR-01.limit: The check did not capture anyone’s password or private traffic.

SL-C01-HSTS-01.title: The browser is not told to always use a secure connection
SL-C01-HSTS-01.what: The HTTPS response is missing an effective Strict-Transport-Security rule.
SL-C01-HSTS-01.why: Someone who can interfere with a visitor’s first insecure connection may try to keep them on HTTP.
SL-C01-HSTS-01.fix: Set a suitable Strict-Transport-Security policy after confirming HTTPS works on the covered hosts.
SL-C01-HSTS-01.limit: This is a missing safeguard. No network interception was demonstrated.

SL-C01-MIXED-01.title: A secure page references an insecure resource
SL-C01-MIXED-01.what: An HTTPS page references active content over HTTP.
SL-C01-MIXED-01.why: If the browser loads that resource, someone controlling its insecure connection could change it. Browsers may block the resource instead.
SL-C01-MIXED-01.fix: Serve all scripts and styles over HTTPS.
SL-C01-MIXED-01.limit: A reference alone does not prove the browser loaded or executed the insecure resource.

SL-C02-COOKIE-02.title: The login cookie is shared with more hosts than necessary
SL-C02-COOKIE-02.what: The cookie’s domain setting makes it available beyond the application that set it.
SL-C02-COOKIE-02.why: A compromised related host may gain access to a shared cookie, depending on the cookie’s scope and protections.
SL-C02-COOKIE-02.fix: Use a host-only cookie unless sharing is required and all covered hosts are trusted.
SL-C02-COOKIE-02.limit: No compromise of a related host was demonstrated.

SL-C04-XCTO-01.title: The browser is missing a rule for handling file types
SL-C04-XCTO-01.what: The response does not set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
SL-C04-XCTO-01.why: In certain content-serving situations, a browser might interpret a file as a more dangerous type than intended.
SL-C04-XCTO-01.fix: Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and send correct Content-Type values.
SL-C04-XCTO-01.limit: A missing setting does not prove uploaded files can run as code.

SL-C05-ERRORS-01.title: An error page reveals internal application details
SL-C05-ERRORS-01.what: A response includes a stack trace or detailed internal error information.
SL-C05-ERRORS-01.why: Someone could use names, paths, and technology details to plan further attacks.
SL-C05-ERRORS-01.fix: Show a generic error page to visitors and keep detailed errors in private logs.
SL-C05-ERRORS-01.limit: An informative error does not prove access to the server.

SL-C05-LISTING-01.title: Visitors can browse a folder’s file list
SL-C05-LISTING-01.what: The server returned a list of files in a directory.
SL-C05-LISTING-01.why: Someone could locate files that were not intended to be easy to find. Whether private data is exposed depends on the files.
SL-C05-LISTING-01.fix: Disable directory listing and remove private files from public folders.
SL-C05-LISTING-01.limit: A file list does not prove every listed file contains sensitive data.

SL-C05-FILES-01.title: A file that should be private is publicly accessible
SL-C05-FILES-01.what: A bounded request returned content matching a sensitive file check.
SL-C05-FILES-01.why: An unauthenticated visitor could read the exposed content. The impact depends on what the saved evidence contains.
SL-C05-FILES-01.fix: Remove the file from public access and rotate any confirmed exposed secrets.
SL-C05-FILES-01.limit: The check does not establish that any exposed credentials are valid or were used.

SL-C05-SECRETS-01.title: Page content contains a possible private credential
SL-C05-SECRETS-01.what: Content delivered to the browser includes a value matching a private-credential pattern.
SL-C05-SECRETS-01.why: If it is a real, active private credential, someone who sees the page may be able to use the access it grants.
SL-C05-SECRETS-01.fix: Identify the value, revoke it if private and active, and keep private credentials on the server.
SL-C05-SECRETS-01.limit: Public identifiers can resemble secrets. The scanner did not use the value to sign in.

SL-C07-METHODS-01.title: The server advertises additional request methods
SL-C07-METHODS-01.what: The server lists methods beyond ordinary page reads.
SL-C07-METHODS-01.why: This is a clue for a permissions review. A listed method is not automatically unsafe.
SL-C07-METHODS-01.fix: Check whether these methods are intended and enforce authorization where needed.
SL-C07-METHODS-01.limit: No unauthorized write or server access was demonstrated.

SL-C07-INVENTORY-01.title: Public API routes were discovered
SL-C07-INVENTORY-01.what: The scan recorded API routes observed on the same website.
SL-C07-INVENTORY-01.why: This helps identify where permissions and input handling need assessment. Discovery alone is not a vulnerability.
SL-C07-INVENTORY-01.fix: Review which routes should be public and assess private routes with authorized test accounts.
SL-C07-INVENTORY-01.limit: A discovered route has not necessarily been tested for access-control flaws.

SL-C03-SQL-01.title: Test inputs indicate a possible database query flaw
SL-C03-SQL-01.what: Repeated controlled input comparisons showed behavior consistent with input changing a database query.
SL-C03-SQL-01.why: If confirmed for this query and permissions, someone may be able to change which database results the application returns. Further access depends on the query and account permissions.
SL-C03-SQL-01.fix: Use parameterized queries and avoid building SQL by joining user input into query text.
SL-C03-SQL-01.limit: The controlled check did not extract a database, bypass a login, or change records.

SL-C03-XSS-01.title: Input can run a script on the page
SL-C03-XSS-01.what: A controlled, harmless script marker ran in the scanner’s browser after input was reflected by the site.
SL-C03-XSS-01.why: A malicious script could act inside the affected page and access data available to that page. The impact depends on the visitor’s permissions and browser protections.
SL-C03-XSS-01.fix: Encode output for its HTML context, use safe DOM APIs, and sanitize content that must contain HTML.
SL-C03-XSS-01.limit: Only the recorded harmless marker and approved test context were checked. No customer account takeover was demonstrated.

SL-C03-DOMXSS-01.title: Page code can turn input into a running script
SL-C03-DOMXSS-01.what: A harmless marker ran through the page’s own browser-side handling of input.
SL-C03-DOMXSS-01.why: A malicious script could act inside the affected page and access data available to that page. The impact depends on the visitor’s permissions and browser protections.
SL-C03-DOMXSS-01.fix: Encode output for its HTML context, use safe DOM APIs, and sanitize content that must contain HTML.
SL-C03-DOMXSS-01.limit: Only the recorded harmless marker and approved test context were checked. No customer account takeover was demonstrated.

SL-C03-STOREDXSS-01.title: Saved input can run a script when another user views it
SL-C03-STOREDXSS-01.what: A controlled marker was stored in a disposable test record and later ran in the designated viewer’s browser.
SL-C03-STOREDXSS-01.why: A malicious script could act inside the affected page and access data available to that page. The impact depends on the visitor’s permissions and browser protections.
SL-C03-STOREDXSS-01.fix: Encode output for its HTML context, use safe DOM APIs, and sanitize content that must contain HTML.
SL-C03-STOREDXSS-01.limit: Only the recorded harmless marker and approved test context were checked. No customer account takeover was demonstrated.

SL-C03-HTML-01.title: Input can change the page’s HTML
SL-C03-HTML-01.what: A harmless input marker became an HTML element rather than plain text.
SL-C03-HTML-01.why: Someone could alter the appearance of the affected page or place misleading content there.
SL-C03-HTML-01.fix: Encode untrusted text before inserting it into HTML.
SL-C03-HTML-01.limit: HTML insertion does not by itself prove script execution.

SL-C04-REDIRECT-01.title: Input can send a visitor to another website
SL-C04-REDIRECT-01.what: A controlled input changed the response’s redirect destination.
SL-C04-REDIRECT-01.why: Someone could use a trusted-looking link to send visitors to a deceptive destination.
SL-C04-REDIRECT-01.fix: Allow only intended redirect destinations, preferably fixed internal paths.
SL-C04-REDIRECT-01.limit: The scanner inspected the redirect and did not follow it to an unapproved website.

SL-C04-CORS-01.title: The response allows unexpected websites to request it
SL-C04-CORS-01.what: The cross-origin response settings accepted a foreign origin with credentials allowed.
SL-C04-CORS-01.why: This can expose private responses if the browser sends credentials and the response actually contains protected data.
SL-C04-CORS-01.fix: Allow only intended origins and avoid credentialed access from arbitrary websites.
SL-C04-CORS-01.limit: Header settings alone do not prove private data is readable by another website.

SL-C04-CORSDATA-01.title: Another website can read a protected test response
SL-C04-CORSDATA-01.what: The approved foreign-page browser check read the protected test marker with credentials.
SL-C04-CORSDATA-01.why: A malicious website could read the affected response when a visitor’s browser supplies the required credentials.
SL-C04-CORSDATA-01.fix: Restrict credentialed cross-origin access to trusted origins.
SL-C04-CORSDATA-01.limit: The evidence covers the declared test response, not all private records on the site.

SL-C04-HDRINJECT-01.title: Input can add an unexpected response header
SL-C04-HDRINJECT-01.what: A harmless input marker created a controlled response header.
SL-C04-HDRINJECT-01.why: Someone might influence how the browser or an intermediary handles that response, depending on which headers can be changed.
SL-C04-HDRINJECT-01.fix: Reject line breaks in header values and use safe response APIs.
SL-C04-HDRINJECT-01.limit: No shared-cache poisoning or harmful browser action was demonstrated.

SL-C08-SESSION-01.title: A login-session protection did not hold
SL-C08-SESSION-01.what: A declared session check found a problem with session replacement, revocation, or expiry. The evidence identifies which test failed.
SL-C08-SESSION-01.why: A still-valid old session may continue to access the account after an event that should invalidate it.
SL-C08-SESSION-01.fix: Replace session identifiers on login and enforce server-side logout and expiry.
SL-C08-SESSION-01.limit: This does not mean passwords were guessed or a login was bypassed. Only the declared session transition was assessed.

SL-C09-OBJECT-01.title: A test account can access another account’s record
SL-C09-OBJECT-01.what: The approved test identity obtained the protected marker for a record it should not access.
SL-C09-OBJECT-01.why: Someone with the tested permissions could access the affected data or operation outside the intended access rules.
SL-C09-OBJECT-01.fix: Check the signed-in user’s permission for every record, field, and operation on the server.
SL-C09-OBJECT-01.limit: The evidence covers the exact declared records and identities. It does not prove access to every account or academic record.

SL-C09-TENANT-01.title: A test account can cross an organization boundary
SL-C09-TENANT-01.what: The approved test identity obtained a protected marker from another declared organization.
SL-C09-TENANT-01.why: Someone with the tested permissions could access the affected data or operation outside the intended access rules.
SL-C09-TENANT-01.fix: Check the signed-in user’s permission for every record, field, and operation on the server.
SL-C09-TENANT-01.limit: The evidence covers the exact declared records and identities. It does not prove access to every account or academic record.

SL-C09-FUNCTION-01.title: A test account can use a restricted operation
SL-C09-FUNCTION-01.what: A lower-permission test identity obtained the protected result of an operation intended for a different role.
SL-C09-FUNCTION-01.why: Someone with the tested permissions could access the affected data or operation outside the intended access rules.
SL-C09-FUNCTION-01.fix: Check the signed-in user’s permission for every record, field, and operation on the server.
SL-C09-FUNCTION-01.limit: The evidence covers the exact declared records and identities. It does not prove access to every account or academic record.

SL-C09-PROPERTY-01.title: A test account can access a restricted record field
SL-C09-PROPERTY-01.what: The approved test identity accessed or changed a field that the declared policy forbids.
SL-C09-PROPERTY-01.why: Someone with the tested permissions could access the affected data or operation outside the intended access rules.
SL-C09-PROPERTY-01.fix: Check the signed-in user’s permission for every record, field, and operation on the server.
SL-C09-PROPERTY-01.limit: The evidence covers the exact declared records and identities. It does not prove access to every account or academic record.

SL-C09-GRAPHQL-01.title: A GraphQL request bypasses a declared access rule
SL-C09-GRAPHQL-01.what: The approved GraphQL test returned a protected marker to a test identity that should not receive it.
SL-C09-GRAPHQL-01.why: Someone with the tested permissions could access the affected data or operation outside the intended access rules.
SL-C09-GRAPHQL-01.fix: Check the signed-in user’s permission for every record, field, and operation on the server.
SL-C09-GRAPHQL-01.limit: The evidence covers the exact declared records and identities. It does not prove access to every account or academic record.

SL-C09-MASS-01.title: An extra input field can change a restricted value
SL-C09-MASS-01.what: A controlled request changed a restricted field on a disposable test record.
SL-C09-MASS-01.why: Someone meeting the tested conditions could cause the affected unauthorized change. The exact changed field or workflow is recorded in the evidence.
SL-C09-MASS-01.fix: Enforce permissions and required workflow steps on the server. For cross-site changes, require anti-CSRF protection and appropriate cookie settings.
SL-C09-MASS-01.limit: Only the declared disposable record and permitted operation were tested. Do not assume marks or attendance were changed unless those exact fields appear in the evidence.

SL-C11-WORKFLOW-01.title: A restricted workflow step can be completed incorrectly
SL-C11-WORKFLOW-01.what: A declared test reached a protected workflow result without satisfying its required role or step.
SL-C11-WORKFLOW-01.why: Someone meeting the tested conditions could cause the affected unauthorized change. The exact changed field or workflow is recorded in the evidence.
SL-C11-WORKFLOW-01.fix: Enforce permissions and required workflow steps on the server. For cross-site changes, require anti-CSRF protection and appropriate cookie settings.
SL-C11-WORKFLOW-01.limit: Only the declared disposable record and permitted operation were tested. Do not assume marks or attendance were changed unless those exact fields appear in the evidence.

SL-C04-CSRF-01.title: Another website can trigger a change in a signed-in session
SL-C04-CSRF-01.what: The approved foreign-page test changed a disposable record using the test session.
SL-C04-CSRF-01.why: Someone meeting the tested conditions could cause the affected unauthorized change. The exact changed field or workflow is recorded in the evidence.
SL-C04-CSRF-01.fix: Enforce permissions and required workflow steps on the server. For cross-site changes, require anti-CSRF protection and appropriate cookie settings.
SL-C04-CSRF-01.limit: Only the declared disposable record and permitted operation were tested. Do not assume marks or attendance were changed unless those exact fields appear in the evidence.

SL-C03-TEMPLATE-01.title: Input may be evaluated as server template code
SL-C03-TEMPLATE-01.what: Controlled comparisons indicated that input was evaluated by the server’s template engine.
SL-C03-TEMPLATE-01.why: Unsafe template evaluation can expose server data or operations, depending on the engine and configuration.
SL-C03-TEMPLATE-01.fix: Keep user input out of template source and pass it only as data.
SL-C03-TEMPLATE-01.limit: The check did not execute operating-system commands.

SL-C10-TRAVERSAL-01.title: A file path can reach outside its intended folder
SL-C10-TRAVERSAL-01.what: The controlled test retrieved an approved canary outside the intended file boundary.
SL-C10-TRAVERSAL-01.why: Someone might read files outside the allowed folder if the same path handling applies to them.
SL-C10-TRAVERSAL-01.fix: Restrict access to a fixed allowed directory and validate resolved paths.
SL-C10-TRAVERSAL-01.limit: Only an approved canary was read. No real private file was retrieved.

SL-C10-UPLOAD-01.title: An uploaded test file was served with an unsafe policy
SL-C10-UPLOAD-01.what: The harmless uploaded test file was served in a way that failed the declared file-serving policy.
SL-C10-UPLOAD-01.why: Certain uploaded content could be interpreted in an unsafe browser context, depending on its type and serving headers.
SL-C10-UPLOAD-01.fix: Validate file types and serve untrusted uploads from an isolated origin with safe headers.
SL-C10-UPLOAD-01.limit: No executable malware or server-code execution was tested.

SL-C05-CACHE-01.title: A protected response crossed a test-session boundary
SL-C05-CACHE-01.what: A controlled cache check returned a private test marker in a context where it should not be shared.
SL-C05-CACHE-01.why: Someone in the tested context could receive data belonging to a different session.
SL-C05-CACHE-01.fix: Keep private responses out of shared caches and include the necessary identity-sensitive cache rules.
SL-C05-CACHE-01.limit: Only the declared private marker and cache scenario were checked.

SL-C07-SSRF-02.title: The server fetched an address supplied in test input
SL-C07-SSRF-02.what: The controlled callback receiver recorded the server’s request to the approved canary.
SL-C07-SSRF-02.why: Someone may be able to make the server contact destinations it should not. Further reach depends on input restrictions and server networking.
SL-C07-SSRF-02.fix: Restrict outbound destinations. Disable external XML entities where applicable.
SL-C07-SSRF-02.limit: The check used an approved canary. It did not retrieve internal services, cloud credentials, or private files.

SL-C03-XXE-02.title: An XML input caused an unexpected external request
SL-C03-XXE-02.what: The controlled XML check caused a request to the approved external canary.
SL-C03-XXE-02.why: Someone may be able to make the server contact destinations it should not. Further reach depends on input restrictions and server networking.
SL-C03-XXE-02.fix: Restrict outbound destinations. Disable external XML entities where applicable.
SL-C03-XXE-02.limit: The check used an approved canary. It did not retrieve internal services, cloud credentials, or private files.

SL-C05-DEBUG-02.title: A public diagnostics page reveals internal details
SL-C05-DEBUG-02.what: The checked diagnostic response included internal information.
SL-C05-DEBUG-02.why: A visitor could read the exposed content without the intended access restriction. What that enables depends on the contents and whether any secrets are still valid.
SL-C05-DEBUG-02.fix: Disable public diagnostics and keep them behind staff-only access.
SL-C05-DEBUG-02.limit: The scanner did not use exposed secrets to log in or compromise another service.

SL-C05-CONFIG-02.title: A configuration backup is publicly readable
SL-C05-CONFIG-02.what: The bounded response matched private configuration content.
SL-C05-CONFIG-02.why: A visitor could read the exposed content without the intended access restriction. What that enables depends on the contents and whether any secrets are still valid.
SL-C05-CONFIG-02.fix: Remove configuration backups from public folders and rotate confirmed exposed secrets.
SL-C05-CONFIG-02.limit: The scanner did not use exposed secrets to log in or compromise another service.

SL-C05-MANAGEMENT-01.title: A management response is publicly readable
SL-C05-MANAGEMENT-01.what: The checked management response exposed data intended for restricted use.
SL-C05-MANAGEMENT-01.why: A visitor could read the exposed content without the intended access restriction. What that enables depends on the contents and whether any secrets are still valid.
SL-C05-MANAGEMENT-01.fix: Restrict management routes to authorized staff and trusted networks.
SL-C05-MANAGEMENT-01.limit: The scanner did not use exposed secrets to log in or compromise another service.

SL-C05-PRIVATE-02.title: A public response contains private key material
SL-C05-PRIVATE-02.what: The bounded response matched private-key material.
SL-C05-PRIVATE-02.why: A visitor could read the exposed content without the intended access restriction. What that enables depends on the contents and whether any secrets are still valid.
SL-C05-PRIVATE-02.fix: Remove public key material immediately and replace the affected key and certificate if exposure is confirmed.
SL-C05-PRIVATE-02.limit: The scanner did not use exposed secrets to log in or compromise another service.

SL-C05-SOURCEMAP-01.title: A public source map contains private material
SL-C05-SOURCEMAP-01.what: The checked source map included material matching a private-content check.
SL-C05-SOURCEMAP-01.why: A visitor could read the exposed content without the intended access restriction. What that enables depends on the contents and whether any secrets are still valid.
SL-C05-SOURCEMAP-01.fix: Remove private data from client builds and rotate any confirmed exposed secrets.
SL-C05-SOURCEMAP-01.limit: The scanner did not use exposed secrets to log in or compromise another service.
